Messages.Author: Stefan Ferenci
Messages.Body:
yesterday during a league game following situation occured:
after ousting my prey and my grand prey i was down on four blood because i
was the target of all the votes of my grand predator. he had 21 pool left
and i had no chance of ousting him. i therefore decided to influence my last
four pool and ousted myself. did i perform an act of unsportmannship
behaviour?

my former grand predator (who is also one of the league organizers) at first
agreed to my actions, but after i put all my cards back into my deck he
claimed i acted against the rules because i played not in order to maximize
my VP´s. he then told me i would be disqualified and my game would be
recorded as a lost because i said that i cannot restore my hand and library.
are his actions right?

stefan

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Stefan Ferenci wrote:
>
> yesterday during a league game following situation occured:
> after ousting my prey and my grand prey i was down on four blood because i
> was the target of all the votes of my grand predator. he had 21 pool left
> and i had no chance of ousting him. i therefore decided to influence my last
> four pool and ousted myself. did i perform an act of unsportmannship
> behaviour?

If it's just the two of you left, you are free to concede at any time.
[VEKN 3.6]

> my former grand predator (who is also one of the league organizers) at first
> agreed to my actions, but after i put all my cards back into my deck he
> claimed i acted against the rules because i played not in order to maximize
> my VP´s. he then told me i would be disqualified and my game would be
> recorded as a lost because i said that i cannot restore my hand and library.
> are his actions right?

It's really up to the league organizer, of course. His actions are "right"
by definition, since it's his league.

If you could not have gained any more VPs by some other course of action,
(as you say) then the assertion that you played not in order to maximize
your VPs is false.

The question is then does the league organizer think you had some way
of gaining VPs at your disposal.

And, if so, does he find that it is appropriate to disqualify you when
he reverses his initial judgement for you having followed his initial
judgment.

--

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Stefan Ferenci wrote:
> is selfousting unsportmanship behaviour? can in not choose the way i want to
> be ousted?

If you have 20 ways in which to gain 0 VPs and no way to gain more than
0 VPs, you may choose any of those 20 ways, including self-ousting,
without being unsporting.

I think what you did was perfectly reasonable. That should teach your
grandpredator from throwing stray vote damage to you!

>my former grand predator (who is also one of the league organizers) at first
>agreed to my actions, but after i put all my cards back into my deck he
>claimed i acted against the rules because i played not in order to maximize
>my VP´s. he then told me i would be disqualified and my game would be
>recorded as a lost because i said that i cannot restore my hand and library.
>are his actions right?

That sounds pretty cheesy. Agreeing with you and once you reach the point of no
return, going back on his decision.

LSJ hath already spoken.

But I think what you did was fine. It *sounds* like you were in a no-win
situation (and I'll assume you were) so yes, you can choose the manner of your
ousting (though Josh and Trey have their own opinions on such matters...).

If anything, it sounds like the tournament organizer was a poor loser who's
just looking for a way to get back at you.

Halcyan 2

If you are actually playing by all of the VEKN tournament rules:
If he is a player in the game, he should not be making any rulings about the
table he is playing at (if multi-judge is being used, he can make rulings
about other tables). This should probably extend to assessing warnings and
disqualifying players at the table he is playing at.

By VEKN tournament rules, there should always be an impartial judge, and if
you are ever in doubt, ask the judge.

Trey
